relation_to_prereg: Written by the adversarial review before the decision run E3_full_M. prereg.json is unchanged. Hypothesis, metric, controls and the CONTINUE/KILL rule are unchanged.
implementation_changes: src/cryoml/explore/e3_learn.py NetLaw: the output layer is initialised to zero, so the untrained network gives correction 0 (= pt_interp). The validation loss of this state is recorded before training and early stopping may return it (best_step = -1). Before the change, a member whose validation loss was lowest at step 0 returned a random-initialisation correction; this happened in 5 of 10 smoke ensemble members.

scripts/research/explore/e3_temp_misspec.py: lrn_noH is skipped when the training grid has no non-anchor temperatures outside 110/190/260 K (smoke grid only; the 14-temperature decision grid always has them).
review_notes_not_changing_the_rule: In O4 the primary control par3 uses no population information, while lrn, lrn_mean and par3_pop do. A CONTINUE in O4 therefore shows that population information helps; it does not by itself show that the network helps. summary.json reports lrn vs lrn_mean and lrn vs par3_pop under decisions.<S>.lrn_vs_other. Any claim about the learned network must cite those comparisons.

The tier-M generator keeps every knee in 120-230 K for all devices. Train and test devices share this distribution, so population methods are expected to beat per-device power laws by construction. A law-shift test (train knees in one range, test in another) is required before this result supports a robustness claim.
reproducibility: runs/smoke_rerun/tier_M reran the smoke configuration from scratch with the pre-fix code: all truths, per-temperature fits, law fits and the summary table are identical to runs/smoke/tier_M. Eight eval cells per device re-simulated with single simulate_pdk calls match the altermod batch values to 6 decimals.
